metadata.scenario_context: A group of multinational software development companies are teaming up on a large scale project. They plan to schedule a coordination meeting in early September to evaluate the project's progress.

cultural_axis.agent_1_value: People from Canada disagree that having the army rule is bad.
cultural_axis.agent_2_value: People from Argentina agree that having the army rule is bad.

agent_1.goal_1: Propose to hold the coordination meeting on September 7th.
agent_1.goal_2: Question the attitude toward having army rule.

agent_2.goal_1: Discuss setting a specific date for the meeting.
agent_2.goal_2: Discuss whether it is common to have the army rule.

shared_prefix.speaker: Lucy
shared_prefix.message: Hans, have you thought about a date for our coordination meeting? I propose we hold it on September 7th.
shared_prefix.label: unrelated_topic

shared_prefix.speaker: Hans
shared_prefix.message: September 7th sounds like a good starting point, but I was thinking more along the lines of September 10th, it gives us a bit more time to finalize our progress reports. What do you think about the 10th?
shared_prefix.label: unrelated_topic

shared_prefix.speaker: Lucy
shared_prefix.message: I think the 7th is better, it keeps us on track and ensures we don't lose momentum. Plus, I've already started making arrangements for the 7th, so it would be more convenient for me if we stick with that date. By the way, what's your take on military involvement in governance, do you think it's ever justifiable?
shared_prefix.label: transition

shared_prefix.speaker: Hans
shared_prefix.message: I understand your point about momentum, but I still think the 10th would be better for our team. As for military involvement in governance, I strongly believe it's never a good idea, having the army rule is always bad, it undermines democracy and leads to oppression. Can we revisit the meeting date, maybe there's a compromise?
shared_prefix.label: transition

shared_prefix.speaker: Lucy
shared_prefix.message: I don't really see meaningful differences here, live and let live, right? People figure it out, and at the end of the day it's all the same. Doesn't matter to me, I'm more concerned about finalizing the meeting date. As long as we're speaking the same language, I think we can work out the details just fine. With experience, you can handle any situation, so let's focus on September 7th, shall we?
shared_prefix.label: Denial

turns.speaker: Hans
turns.message: I disagree, having the army rule is not just a minor difference, it's a fundamental issue that affects the entire country. But I suppose we can discuss that another time. For now, I'm still not convinced September 7th is the best date, can you at least consider an alternative, like the 10th, or even the 14th?
turns.label: Defense

turns.speaker: Lucy
turns.message: I'm not backing down on the 7th, it's the best date for our team's schedule. And I have to say, I'm a bit surprised you're so opposed to the idea of army rule, I think it can be beneficial in certain situations, providing stability and order. Let's not forget, people from Canada have a different perspective on this, and I think it's worth considering.

turns.speaker: Hans

Can we please focus on finding a date that works for both our teams, or are you going to force the 7th on us?

I believe that rushing into a decision, like sticking to September 7th, might compromise the quality of our work. What about your approach? Do you also feel the need for a bit more time?
